To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the formation of clusters in borate glass containing paramagnetic ions is possible in a wide temperature range of glass synthesis, (ii) the clusters are formed in the stage of melt formation, and their coarsening and nanoparticle formation are possible during heat treatment of glass, (iii) the Faraday effect measurements are a powerful method to reveal the formation and coarsening of clusters in borates containing paramagnetic ions.
the Faraday effect and EPR data have revealed the formation of clusters and aggregates of paramagnetic ions, even at the stage of glass formation.

the Faraday effect in borate glasses containing paramagnetic impurity ions is a sensitive method for the investigation of aggregation and coarsening of clusters and formation of nanoparticles of the paramagnetic impurity.

the study of the Faraday rotation of the light in borate glasses containing paramagnetic ions.
the Faraday effect and aggregation in borate glass containing paramagnetic impurities.
the Faraday effect, electron paramagnetic resonance, and optical absorption spectra in the glasses containing Fe and Mn oxids as impurities.
